body:
The registry ("all items ever seen", reached from the list's top bar) renders whatever order
SQLite happens to return -- Daos.searchRegistry has no ORDER BY at all, so the order is
effectively insertion order and formally unspecified. On a list with any history that makes
finding a known item a scan rather than a lookup.

Sort by name, case-insensitively.

Sorted in RegistryViewModel with a java.text.Collator rather than in SQL: SQLite's
COLLATE NOCASE only case-folds ASCII, so in any of the eight non-English locales this app
ships, accented and non-Latin names would sort by code point -- "Apfel", "Butter", "Zucker",
"Äpfel". A registry is one list's items, so sorting it in memory is cheap.
title: Android: the registry lists items in no particular order
